title: Upstream rejected branch/path-derived capture identity for linked-worktree evidence (PR #173)
observation: davesheffer/hunch PR #173 ('refuse a decision/correction/finding capture whose file evidence points at a linked worktree', branch worktree-misroute-guard) was closed by David Sheffer on 2026-09-14 rather than merged, with a specific rejection of its approach: deriving capture identity from branch name / file path causes a production regression — a decision's identity changes after a branch rename or merge, while unrelated clones on the same branch can still collide. The PR's filename/history heuristic also both rejects valid root captures and misses real worktree-only evidence; newline-bearing paths parse incorrectly; and the synchronous per-path git history scan can block the MCP server. Stated replacement direction (not yet landed in upstream/main as of this check): keep Hunch's existing semantic, clone-stable IDs and explicit cwd routing, carry the exact working directory through native prompt/subagent flows, and fail closed only when write provenance is genuinely ambiguous. Checked upstream/main at commit 30775928 (fetched 2026-09-14) — no decision, correction, or finding in .hunch/ records this rationale or a landed fix matching it; two superficially related commits (db21d3f4/dec_ad581587cf, c2203ab4/dec_c561c277db, both ~00:35 UTC same day) fix a different thing (comparing worktree roots by physical Git directory identity in tooling/development-run.mjs), not MCP capture-identity/cwd routing.
